questions.question: What is the time complexity to access an element in an array given its index?
options: O(log n)
O(n)

questions.question: Which searching algorithm sequentially checks each element of a list until a match is found or the whole list has been searched?
options: Binary search
Linear search
Interpolation search
Exponential search

questions.question: What is the primary prerequisite for applying standard binary search directly on an array?
options: The array elements must be distinct.
The array size must be an exact power of 2.
The array must be sorted in a monotonic order.
The array must contain only positive integers.

questions.question: Consider the array [64, 25, 12, 22, 11]. After the first complete pass of standard Selection Sort (finding the minimum element and placing it at the beginning), what is the state of the array?
Which sorting algorithm achieves an optimal best-case time complexity of O(n) when provided with an array that is already completely sorted in ascending order?
options: Standard Selection Sort
Standard Merge Sort
Insertion Sort
Quick Sort with first element as pivot

questions.question: An array contains elements [3, 7, 12, 19, 24, 31, 45, 52]. If Binary Search is used to search for the target value 24, which sequence of middle elements will be examined? (Assume integer division mid = (low + high) / 2).
What is the total auxiliary (extra) space complexity of standard recursive Merge Sort on an array of size n?
options: O(log n)
O(n)
O(n log n)

questions.question: In an array of size n containing both positive and negative integers, which approach is most optimal in terms of both time and auxiliary space to segregate even and odd numbers in-place?
options: Two-pointer technique with left and right indices moving toward each other in O(n) time and O(1) space.
Sorting the entire array using Merge Sort in O(n log n) time and O(n) space.
Creating a secondary temporary array and copying elements in O(n) time and O(n) space.
Nested loops comparing every pair in O(n^2) time and O(1) space.

questions.question: What is the recurrence relation that represents the worst-case time complexity of standard Quick Sort when the partition always results in unbalanced subproblems of sizes 0 and n - 1?

Given an array sorted in non-decreasing order that contains duplicate elements, which modified binary search condition correctly updates the pointers to find the first occurrence (lower bound index) of a target value?
options: If arr[mid] == target, return mid immediately.
If arr[mid] == target, set low = mid + 1.
If arr[mid] >= target, record potential answer and set high = mid - 1.
If arr[mid] <= target, record potential answer and set low = mid + 1.

questions.question: A sorting algorithm is considered 'stable' if:
options: It runs in O(n log n) time across all test cases.
It maintains the relative order of duplicate elements with equal keys.
It sorts the array without requiring any auxiliary memory.
Its best-case and worst-case time complexities are identical.

questions.question: You are given a sorted array of distinct integers that has been rotated at an unknown pivot (for example, [4, 5, 6, 7, 0, 1, 2]). How can you search for a target value in O(log n) time?
options: Perform linear search from both ends simultaneously.
In binary search, identify which half ([low..mid] or [mid..high]) is normally sorted, and check if the target falls within that sorted range.
Sort the rotated array back to its original order using Insertion Sort, then run binary search.
Find the maximum element using linear search in O(n), then binary search each half separately.

questions.question: Given an array of n integers and a target sum k, you need to find two distinct indices whose elements sum to k. If the array is already sorted, what is the most optimal time and auxiliary space complexity to determine if such a pair exists?
options: O(n log n) time and O(1) space
O(n) time and O(n) space
O(n) time and O(1) space
O(n^2) time and O(1) space
It throws an array out of bounds error for any valid target.
When arr[mid] > target, passing mid instead of mid - 1 can lead to infinite recursion when low == high.
The calculation low + (high - low) / 2 causes an integer overflow.
It fails to search the right half of the array properly.

questions.question: What is the maximum number of recursive stack frames active at any one time during a standard recursive Quick Sort of an array with n distinct elements in the worst case?
options: O(log n)
O(n)
O(n log n)

questions.question: You are given an array of size n containing integers from the range 1 to n - 1 such that exactly one number is duplicated. If modifying the array is forbidden and you must use O(1) auxiliary space and O(n) time, which technique should you apply?
options: Two pointers from left and right on a sorted copy
Floyd's Tortoise and Hare (Cycle Detection) viewing the array indices and values as a linked list
Binary search on index positions from 0 to n - 1
Nested loops to compare each pair

questions.question: We want to find the square root of a non-negative integer x rounded down to the nearest integer using binary search over the search space [0, x]. Which condition determines whether mid is the integer square root?
options: mid * mid == x only
mid * mid <= x and (mid + 1) * (mid + 1) > x
mid <= x / 2
(mid - 1) * (mid - 1) <= x and mid * mid >= x

questions.question: Consider an array where every element is at most k positions away from its target position in the sorted array (an 'almost sorted' or k-sorted array). What is the minimum time complexity required to sort this array?
options: O(n)
O(n log k)
O(k log n)
O(n log n)

questions.question: You are given an infinite/unbounded sorted array of positive integers where the length is unknown. How can you find the position of a given key in O(log p) time, where p is the actual position of the key?
options: Scan sequentially until arr[i] > key, then stop.
Find a bounding range [low, high] by exponentially doubling the index (1, 2, 4, 8, ...) until arr[high] >= key, then perform binary search within [high/2, high].
Estimate the size using a large constant like 10^9 and execute standard binary search.
Apply ternary search starting from index 0.

questions.question: Given two sorted arrays A of size m and B of size n, which approach finds the median of the merged array in O(log(min(m, n))) time?
options: Merge both arrays into a temporary array of size m + n, then access the middle element.

Run binary search on the partition index of the smaller array such that the total number of elements on the left halves of both arrays equals the total on the right halves, and max(left) <= min(right).
Run two pointers from the beginning of both arrays and count up to (m + n) / 2 elements.
Concatenate A and B, apply Quickselect to locate the median element.
